Buffer overflow in image processing causing remote code execution or DoS — An attacker crafts an image to cause buffer overflow in image processing, leading to potential remote code execution, denial of service, and errors.
Supply chain attack on third-party libraries compromising system outputs — An attacker poisons the supply chain of third-party libraries, leading to network or system compromise.
Image Tampering — An attacker tampers with or deletes stored images to impact training or testing results and/or cause denial of service.
Notebook tampering to insert a backdoor — An attacker modifies a notebook file to insert a backdoor, such as a keylogger or data stealer.
Machine learning model tampering causing low accuracy or IP theft — An attacker or insider modifies or reads persisted model files to steal intellectual property or degrade prediction accuracy.
Image perturbation attack resulting in incorrect classifications — An attacker uses brute force with random or systematic perturbations to create images that lead to incorrect classifications.
Sensitive image exposure due to accidental access — An attacker or malicious insider gains access to sensitive uploaded images.
SSH compromise via stolen credentials from developer machine — An attacker compromises a developer machine to steal SSH keys, impersonate users, or escalate privileges.
SSH compromise via open port vulnerability — An attacker exploits an open SSH port to escalate privileges or impersonate authorized users.
